requirements.quote:
After the initial HEADERS frame sent by each peer, all subsequent
   DATA frames correspond to data sent on the TCP connection.  The frame
   payload of any DATA frames sent by the client is transmitted by the
   proxy to the TCP server; data received from the TCP server is
   assembled into DATA frames by the proxy.  Frame types other than DATA
   or stream management frames (RST_STREAM, WINDOW_UPDATE, and PRIORITY)
   MUST NOT be sent on a connected stream and MUST be treated as a
   stream error (Section 5.4.2) if received.
requirements.condition: After each peer has sent the initial HEADERS frame on a connected stream.
requirements.required_behavior: All subsequent DATA frames correspond to data sent on the TCP connection.
requirements.why_checkable: A frame trace can verify that post-HEADERS DATA payloads correspond to tunneled TCP data.

After the initial HEADERS frame sent by each peer, all subsequent

requirements.condition: A proxy receives a client DATA frame on a connected stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Transmit the DATA frame payload to the TCP server.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can compare client DATA payloads with bytes transmitted by the proxy to the TCP server.

requirements.quote:
After the initial HEADERS frame sent by each peer, all subsequent
   DATA frames correspond to data sent on the TCP connection.  The frame
   payload of any DATA frames sent by the client is transmitted by the
   proxy to the TCP server; data received from the TCP server is

requirements.condition: A proxy receives data from the TCP server for a connected stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Assemble the received TCP data into DATA frames.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can supply TCP bytes and inspect the proxy's resulting HTTP/2 DATA frames.

requirements.quote:
After the initial HEADERS frame sent by each peer, all subsequent
   DATA frames correspond to data sent on the TCP connection.  The frame
   payload of any DATA frames sent by the client is transmitted by the
   proxy to the TCP server; data received from the TCP server is
   assembled into DATA frames by the proxy.  Frame types other than DATA
   or stream management frames (RST_STREAM, WINDOW_UPDATE, and PRIORITY)
   MUST NOT be sent on a connected stream and MUST be treated as a
   stream error (Section 5.4.2) if received.
requirements.condition: A stream is connected after the initial HEADERS frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send frame types other than DATA, RST_STREAM, WINDOW_UPDATE, or PRIORITY on the connected stream.
requirements.why_checkable: An emitted-frame trace can be checked against the closed set of permitted frame types.

requirements.quote:
After the initial HEADERS frame sent by each peer, all subsequent
   DATA frames correspond to data sent on the TCP connection.  The frame
   payload of any DATA frames sent by the client is transmitted by the
   proxy to the TCP server; data received from the TCP server is
   assembled into DATA frames by the proxy.  Frame types other than DATA
   or stream management frames (RST_STREAM, WINDOW_UPDATE, and PRIORITY)
   MUST NOT be sent on a connected stream and MUST be treated as a
   stream error (Section 5.4.2) if received.
requirements.condition: A frame other than DATA, RST_STREAM, WINDOW_UPDATE, or PRIORITY is received on a connected stream.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat receipt as a stream error.
requirements.why_checkable: A peer can inject each prohibited frame type and verify that the implementation raises a stream-level error.

requirements.quote:
The TCP connection can be closed by either peer.  The END_STREAM flag
   on a DATA frame is treated as being equivalent to the TCP FIN bit.  A
   client is expected to send a DATA frame with the END_STREAM flag set
   after receiving a frame with the END_STREAM flag set.  A proxy that
   receives a DATA frame with the END_STREAM flag set sends the attached
   data with the FIN bit set on the last TCP segment.  A proxy that
   receives a TCP segment with the FIN bit set sends a DATA frame with
   the END_STREAM flag set.  Note that the final TCP segment or DATA
   frame could be empty.
requirements.condition: A client receives a frame with the END_STREAM flag set on a connected stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a DATA frame with the END_STREAM flag set.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver peer END_STREAM and observe whether the client subsequently closes its sending side with END_STREAM on DATA.

requirements.quote:
The TCP connection can be closed by either peer.  The END_STREAM flag
   on a DATA frame is treated as being equivalent to the TCP FIN bit.  A
   client is expected to send a DATA frame with the END_STREAM flag set
   after receiving a frame with the END_STREAM flag set.  A proxy that
   receives a DATA frame with the END_STREAM flag set sends the attached
   data with the FIN bit set on the last TCP segment.  A proxy that
   receives a TCP segment with the FIN bit set sends a DATA frame with
   the END_STREAM flag set.  Note that the final TCP segment or DATA
   frame could be empty.
requirements.condition: A proxy receives a DATA frame with the END_STREAM flag set.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the attached data to the TCP peer with the FIN bit set on the last TCP segment.
requirements.why_checkable: The proxy's TCP output can be inspected to verify payload forwarding and FIN placement on the last segment.

requirements.quote:
The TCP connection can be closed by either peer.  The END_STREAM flag
   on a DATA frame is treated as being equivalent to the TCP FIN bit.  A
   client is expected to send a DATA frame with the END_STREAM flag set
   after receiving a frame with the END_STREAM flag set.  A proxy that
   receives a DATA frame with the END_STREAM flag set sends the attached
   data with the FIN bit set on the last TCP segment.  A proxy that
   receives a TCP segment with the FIN bit set sends a DATA frame with
   the END_STREAM flag set.  Note that the final TCP segment or DATA
   frame could be empty.
requirements.condition: A proxy receives a TCP segment with the FIN bit set.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a DATA frame with the END_STREAM flag set.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inject a TCP FIN and inspect the corresponding HTTP/2 DATA frame flags.

requirements.quote:
The TCP connection can be closed by either peer.  The END_STREAM flag
   on a DATA frame is treated as being equivalent to the TCP FIN bit.  A
   client is expected to send a DATA frame with the END_STREAM flag set
   after receiving a frame with the END_STREAM flag set.  A proxy that
   receives a DATA frame with the END_STREAM flag set sends the attached
   data with the FIN bit set on the last TCP segment.  A proxy that
   receives a TCP segment with the FIN bit set sends a DATA frame with
   the END_STREAM flag set.  Note that the final TCP segment or DATA
   frame could be empty.
requirements.condition: A proxy translates connection closure between TCP FIN and DATA END_STREAM.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the final TCP segment or final DATA frame to have an empty payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reject or omit a valid empty final TCP segment or DATA frame solely because it is empty.
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary tests can close an otherwise payload-free tunnel and verify that empty terminal units are accepted and propagated.

requirements.quote:
A TCP connection error is signaled with RST_STREAM.  A proxy treats
   any error in the TCP connection, which includes receiving a TCP
   segment with the RST bit set, as a stream error (Section 5.4.2) of
   type CONNECT_ERROR.  Correspondingly, a proxy MUST send a TCP segment
   with the RST bit set if it detects an error with the stream or the
   HTTP/2 connection.
requirements.condition: A proxy encounters any error in the TCP connection, including receipt of a TCP segment with the RST bit set.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the condition as a stream error of type CONNECT_ERROR and signal the TCP connection error with RST_STREAM.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can induce TCP failures or TCP RST and inspect the resulting HTTP/2 stream error and error code.

requirements.quote:
A TCP connection error is signaled with RST_STREAM.  A proxy treats
   any error in the TCP connection, which includes receiving a TCP
   segment with the RST bit set, as a stream error (Section 5.4.2) of
   type CONNECT_ERROR.  Correspondingly, a proxy MUST send a TCP segment
   with the RST bit set if it detects an error with the stream or the
   HTTP/2 connection.
requirements.condition: A proxy detects an error with the connected stream or the HTTP/2 connection.
requirements.error_behavior: Send a TCP segment with the RST bit set.
requirements.why_checkable: Stream and connection faults can be injected and the TCP side observed for an RST.

requirements.quote:
HTTP/2 does not support the 101 (Switching Protocols) informational
   status code (Section 15.2.2 of [HTTP]).
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use or accept the 101 (Switching Protocols) informational status code as a supported HTTP/2 status code.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation's encoder and response handling can be tested with status code 101.

requirements.quote:
*  The GOAWAY frame indicates the highest stream number that might
      have been processed.  Requests on streams with higher numbers are
      therefore guaranteed to be safe to retry.
requirements.condition: A GOAWAY frame is received with a last-stream identifier.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat requests on streams with identifiers higher than the indicated stream number as unprocessed and safe to retry.
requirements.why_checkable: A client can be given GOAWAY and checked for retry eligibility decisions on streams above the advertised identifier.

requirements.quote:
*  The REFUSED_STREAM error code can be included in a RST_STREAM
      frame to indicate that the stream is being closed prior to any
      processing having occurred.  Any request that was sent on the
      reset stream can be safely retried.
requirements.condition: A stream is reset with RST_STREAM carrying REFUSED_STREAM.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the stream as closed before processing and its request as safe to retry.
requirements.why_checkable: A client can receive REFUSED_STREAM and its retry classification can be observed.

requirements.quote:
Requests that have not been processed have not failed; clients MAY
   automatically retry them, even those with non-idempotent methods.
requirements.condition: A request is known not to have been processed.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the client to retry the request automatically, including when its method is non-idempotent.
requirements.why_checkable: A client retry policy can be tested after an unprocessed-request indication for both idempotent and non-idempotent methods.

requirements.quote:
A server MUST NOT indicate that a stream has not been processed
   unless it can guarantee that fact.  If frames that are on a stream
   are passed to the application layer for any stream, then
   REFUSED_STREAM MUST NOT be used for that stream, and a GOAWAY frame
   MUST include a stream identifier that is greater than or equal to the
   given stream identifier.
requirements.condition: A server cannot guarantee that a stream has not been processed.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Indicate that the stream has not been processed.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can correlate server processing state with emitted REFUSED_STREAM or GOAWAY indications.

requirements.quote:
A server MUST NOT indicate that a stream has not been processed
   unless it can guarantee that fact.  If frames that are on a stream
   are passed to the application layer for any stream, then
   REFUSED_STREAM MUST NOT be used for that stream, and a GOAWAY frame
   MUST include a stream identifier that is greater than or equal to the
   given stream identifier.
requirements.condition: Frames on a stream have been passed to the application layer.
requirements.why_checkable: Instrumentation can establish application delivery and verify that the server never resets that stream with REFUSED_STREAM.

requirements.quote:
A server MUST NOT indicate that a stream has not been processed
   unless it can guarantee that fact.  If frames that are on a stream
   are passed to the application layer for any stream, then
   REFUSED_STREAM MUST NOT be used for that stream, and a GOAWAY frame
   MUST include a stream identifier that is greater than or equal to the
   given stream identifier.
requirements.condition: Frames on a stream have been passed to the application layer and the server sends GOAWAY.
requirements.required_behavior: Include a stream identifier greater than or equal to that stream's identifier in the GOAWAY frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can record the application-delivered stream identifier and compare it with the last-stream identifier in GOAWAY.
